correctness.rationale: For the rule image displayed in Fellin Definition 2.3, applying the sequent maps twice to each member of the premise set and to the conclusion is precisely the direct image under the composite. This also proves the rule-package union identity, including duplicate images or empty premises. On concrete sequents the soundness implication and the faithfulness implication compose in opposite directions; the identity and associativity are pointwise. This proves the two category statements in the source convention. Premise indexes are subsets of N. Literal equality concerns the displayed image operation, not an additional theorem that arbitrary list maps commute with metavariable substitution or map instances to instances; no such extension to independently interpreted open expressions is justified. The bound verification is analytic and does not supply a formal certificate.

evidence: Fellin's Proposition 2.5 treats one-stage translated-calculus soundness and minimality; Definitions 2.3–2.4 use arbitrary calculi under the source convention.
The earlier nuclei paper treats abstract single-conclusion consequence and composition of compatible rules, rather than arbitrary two-sided list-map translations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither the unrelated compatible-rule composition nor a stronger proof-theoretic meta-theorem is needed; the cited arbitrary-calculus definitions themselves are sufficient for the broadest stated scope.

evidence: For any two maps F and G on sequents and any premise set P, G[F[P]]=(G∘F)[P] by element membership; the conclusion under either side is G(F(c)). Direct image also preserves union. The two implications of Definition 2.4 compose, and componentwise identity and associativity are automatic.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This explicitly derives not just a related one-stage result but every asserted equality and the finite-chain statement from the source definitions.

evidence: Encode a rule as a pair consisting of a set of premises and one conclusion. Definition 2.3 acts by direct image and by evaluation respectively; ordinary direct image already has the claimed composition law.
Soundness and faithfulness are preservation and reflection of the unary predicate of derivability. Dvorkin uses an iff for formula-level exact interpretations, not Fellin rule packages.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In the sets-and-predicate formulation, the category and its wide subcategory are consequences of the standard preservation/reflection implications. No structural property of derivability is used.

evidence: The closest catalogue record gives a multiplication table of five normal modal-to-modal translation classes modulo target equivalence and an explicit formula-composition identity. It does not tabulate or state arbitrary rule images.
There is no separate numerical invariant or enumeration in this record; its exact output is the displayed identity, tested against the literal rule-image definition.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The modal table is not the same result. The exact strict identity is nonetheless a direct consequence of the prior rule schema formula.

originality.rationale: The exact wording need not occur in Fellin: Definitions 2.3–2.4 already mechanically entail the whole conjunction by ordinary direct-image composition, union preservation and transitivity of implication. No extra hypothesis or non-definitional assertion distinguishes the finding.
residual_risks: The bounded reading does not settle who first wrote the categorical observation explicitly; the failure is based on demonstrated prior implication, not the absence or presence of matching wording.

value.rationale: The observation may orient a reader, but it is ordinary direct-image functoriality plus two implication chains. No new rule admissibility, conservation, substitution interaction, obstruction or nontrivial classification is obtained; the same immediate calculation already flattens any well-typed finite chain. There is no surviving substantive result to repair.
